analysis.investment_thesis: Fedbank Financial Services is an NBFC — a financial company that the Magic Formula explicitly excludes because debt is the raw material of its business, making EBIT/EV and ROIC meaningless. Even setting that aside, a declining earnings year (FY25 net profit INR 225 Cr vs INR 245 Cr in FY24) and ROE of only 8.84% do not clear Greenblatt's bar.
key_strengths: Strong revenue CAGR of 32.2% (FY22–25) shows the loan book is scaling rapidly
Promoter stake of 60.79% (Federal Bank parent) provides institutional credibility and funding access
Forward P/E of 11.35x suggests the market is pricing in earnings recovery — cheap on stated earnings
key_risks: ROE of 8.84% is well below my 20%+ ROIC threshold — this is not a high-quality compounder
Earnings are actually shrinking: net profit fell from INR 245 Cr (FY24) to INR 225 Cr (FY25) — negative growth momentum
D/E of 3.83x is structurally necessary for an NBFC, but leaves zero margin of safety if credit quality deteriorates
red_flags: Financial company — Magic Formula is explicitly inapplicable; EBIT/EV and ROIC metrics are distorted by leverage that is core to operations
Operating CF negative all 4 years (-978 Cr in FY25); FCF negative every year — cash is consumed, not generated

Finance cost data (INR 12 Cr) appears inconsistent with INR 10,437 Cr of debt — suggests reported 'revenue' may be net interest income, understating true cost structure and making margin metrics unreliable
Operating income also declined YoY (INR 337 Cr FY24 → INR 316 Cr FY25) — revenue growth is not converting to profit growth
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula starts and ends with one hard rule: exclude financial companies. Fedbank Financial Services is an NBFC — it borrows money to lend it out. Debt (INR 10,437 Cr) is not a liability to be subtracted from enterprise value; it IS the business. This means EBIT/EV is a fiction, and ROIC (EBIT / Net Working Capital + Net Fixed Assets) captures nothing meaningful when the loan book is the only real asset. No ranking, no comparison, no formula output is valid here. I simply cannot run the screen.

Looking past the formula, the underlying business quality is mediocre. ROE of 8.84% means Fedfina earns less than 9 cents on every rupee of equity — I want businesses earning 20–25%+. More worrying, despite 30%+ revenue CAGR, profits actually shrank in FY25 (net profit –8.2% YoY, operating income –6.2% YoY), suggesting rising credit costs or funding pressures are eroding the spread. The data anomaly around finance costs (INR 12 Cr on INR 10,437 Cr of debt is a ~0.1% borrowing cost — impossible) further reduces confidence in the reported margins. There is no Magic Formula case here, and no compelling general-value case either.
